candidates.title: Europe’s container ports: Why is transshipment falling while gateway traffic grows?
candidates.excerpt: Europe’s major container ports are reporting increasingly contrasting traffic patterns in 2026, with headline throughput figures concealing significant changes in the composition of cargo flows. At Rotterdam and Valencia, transshipment volumes have declined substantially during the first nine months of the year, while traffic linked to imports and inland markets has strengthened. Antwerp-Bruges presents a different picture, with modest overall container growth driven by empty rather than full containers. The figures raise an important question for Europe’s port sector: are changes in terminal capacity, cargo demand and shipping networks altering the balance between transshipment and gateway activity? The available evidence points to changes at individual ports rather than a confirmed Europe-wide shift. candidates.title: Commissioners approve new rail line to Port of Moses Lake, Wash.
candidates.excerpt: MOSES LAKE, Wash. — Port of Moses Lake commissioners have approved a contract to build a new rail line connecting the port to the Columbia Basin Railroad. The Hagadone News Network reports that commissioners approved a $31.75 million contract with Martinus Rail LLC North America to build the connection at their meeting on Monday, Oct. 26. Construction could begin as early as next month, with completion projected in spring 2028. The Northern Columbia Basin Rail Project, designed to restore rail service that was lost in 2009, will include construction of 4.7 miles of new railroad and improvements to 2.7 miles of existing track. The port estimates it will initially generate round-trip service for 10 cars per week, growing to a daily round trip by 2045. Six companies responded to the request for bids issued in September; all six came in below the port’s estimated cost of $40 million to $47.5 million. Carloads totaled 232,120 units, up 3.5%, and intermodal volume of 308,015 containers and trailers was 12.6% better y/y. Nine of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. Metallic ores and metals used in steelmaking and other production led all gainers, up 14.5%.
